title: fix(tests): pass private cache policy to Python descendants
body:
The isolated unittest process has a private `-X pycache_prefix`, but that interpreter option does not reach Python children launched by tests. A stale child import can therefore make a current-source failure pass. This passes each module's owned cache prefix and no-write policy through its child environment, retaining explicit interpreter commands, completion receipts, output ordering and process cleanup.

The source-bound package runs the unchanged existing source-history CLI test. In a disposable fixture, the original three-field parser is cached and current source is changed from 3 to 4. The old runner passes with timestamp or unchecked-hash bytecode and fails after only the cache is removed; the successor reports the current-source failure throughout. No mathematical certificate bypass is claimed.

Validation:

- Sixteen CLI differential runs, including clean/source-only, external-prefix, checked-hash, unchanged-byte and cleanup controls; also pass under optimized Python 3.12 and 3.14.
- Eleven public-CLI bytecode groups pass on Python 3.11/3.12/3.14; 38 tests pass through actual runner integration. Isolated suite: 34 pass, 14 existing platform skips.
- Registered new and PR2990 predecessor package replays pass. Metadata/pins, committed bytes and source-history ancestry pass.
- Historical suite: 25/27 pass. The two remaining failures concern the **unchanged** `docs/ci-verification.md` allowlist; the exact rejection also occurs using canonical main's original checker/document/manifest. This admits only the new runner digest and preserves the historical original. Details and exact hashes are in TASK/README.

The deliberately unprotected registered-interpreter test control now explicitly removes inherited cache isolation, retaining its original failure assertion. `-I`/`-E`, explicit child overrides, custom loaders and concurrent source mutation remain outside this fix; an actual `-I` control demonstrates that limit. No native Windows/Linux, hosted CI, full selected replay, supplier or κ claim.

Entry and final canonical main: `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`, priority revision 6. Final overlap completely paginated 261 open PRs and 2191 Discussion/comment/reply records without warnings. No competing descendant-import claim was found; arbitrary diffs, unpublished work and remote closed PR bodies remain outside coverage. Scientific commit: `2824fc68ffe792a3d8060f4acaea88f1fc123df4`.

Credit Nick Petalas for PR2990, the explicit descendant handoff, and the source-history checker/test; PR2553/frame-closure-child-isolation for earlier cache boundaries; Dennis, Douglas Colkitt and the retained runner/completion/concurrency/process-lifecycle lineage. Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; author-checked, no independent human or subagent review claimed. Apache-2.0. Selected frontier and frozen packages unchanged.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2988#discussioncomment-19007616
Replay: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/isolated-descendant-bytecode`

Next: review the inherited-environment contract and address the unrelated document-pin debt separately. An explicitly isolated child needs its own named caller/fixture before any further import-policy expansion.
